text:
lex: Heads-up — bringing up a converted Llama->Mistral variant (titus-3b-conv) on int4 and seeing a small but consistent embed offset that only shows up past ~2048 tokens. perplexity jumps and a few hallucinations in summarization tests. anyone seen this pattern?

sasha: can you paste the minimal repro? is it only when quantized or also float32?

lex: repro is quick:
```bash
# convert weights with our converter v2
./convert_weights --src llama3-titus --dst mistralish --out /tmp/titus-mistral
# serve with int4 profile
./redwood-run --model /tmp/titus-mistral --quant int4 --max-tokens 4096
# run eval suite
python eval_long_context.py --endpoint localhost:8080 --prompts tests/long_summaries.json
```
outputs show token-level embedding mismatch in the first kv cache refill after 2048. float32 run (no quant) looks fine.

tom: throwing the first diff here — looks like the kv cache ids line up but the attention scores shift by one head in some layers. snippet: 
```
layer 6 head 3 attn_sum[0:8] (float32): [0.12, 0.05, 0.03,...]
layer 6 head 3 attn_sum[0:8] (int4):   [0.05, 0.03, 0.12,...]
```

ama: my gut says a head-permutation or transpose got applied when we fused rotary + grouped heads during quant kernel lowering. Gemma conversions historically had a head-ordering mismatch when we switched the per-head layout. Could be the same class of bug but triggered only when quantized due to packing losing an implicit reorder.

lex: that matches what i suspected. i also noticed Qwen-style tokenizer aliasing in this model conversion; token ids > 65000 got remapped and we do a cheap modulo in the converter. might be unrelated but worth checking.

sasha: quick bisect plan: (1) run float32 with converter v2 and v1; (2) run int4 with kernel fuser on/off; (3) re-run with head-perm shim that forces [h, d]->[d, h] canonicalization. can automate.

lex: started (1) and (2) locally, pushing logs: 
```
# logs excerpt
2026-03-20T10:12:11Z converter v2 -> success
2026-03-20T10:13:08Z runtime int4 kernel fused=true -> perf ok, but embed-offset observed
2026-03-20T10:15:42Z runtime int4 kernel fused=false -> no offset (surprising)
```

ama: if fused=false removes the offset, then the fusion pass is reordering heads incorrectly when lowering quant kernels. i can add an assert to the fusion step to validate head strides and rotary dims.

ci-bot: unit-tests/int4_fusion/headstride_check started by lex (job #4821).

tom: small experiment: applied head-perm shim at runtime and re-ran int4 fused -> offset disappeared. seems deterministic.

lex: ok great — let's make a short PR to add a protective check in the fuser and a fallback path (skip fusion if layout ambiguous). i'll open it and tag ama for review.

ops-bot: FYI — if we ship a rollback, Dedicated clusters with reserved capacity will be routed to float32 fallback until PR lands.

ama: i'll draft the fuser guard and a small reproducer test for the long-context eval suite. we should also audit converter for the token-id aliasing lex mentioned. separate follow-up ticket. :memo:

sasha: sounds good. lex can you attach a tiny reproducer (200 lines) to the ticket? helps SRE to stress test.

lex: will do — uploading now to the ticket. thanks all :thumbsup:
